title: Preparation of Alkanes Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Cooking gas, petrol and candle wax look nothing alike, yet all are made of only carbon and hydrogen. In this animated lesson that opens Class 11 Chemistry Chapter 9 (Hydrocarbons), Aarav oils his bicycle chain and meets the same family.

You will see hydrocarbons classified (saturated alkanes, unsaturated alkenes and alkynes, cycloalkanes and aromatic), the rule CnH2n+2 and why alkanes were called paraffins. Then four ways to make alkanes, built on the molecule bench: hydrogenation over Pt, Pd or Ni with H2 splitting on the metal, reduction of alkyl halides with Zn and HCl, the Wurtz reaction, decarboxylation with soda lime and Kolbe's electrolysis. A carbon counting worked example, the Wurtz mixture trap, an original NEET pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

This is Episode 89 of our PUC Chemistry series. 

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Cooking gas, petrol and wax
0:22 Classification of hydrocarbons
0:50 CnH2n+2 and paraffins
1:06 Hydrogenation live on the bench
1:41 From alkyl halides: Zn and HCl, Wurtz
2:09 Decarboxylation and Kolbe's electrolysis
2:49 Wurtz vs decarboxylation, pause and think
3:20 Worked example: count the carbons
3:40 Exam trap: Wurtz with two halides
4:04 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:40 Recap and three questions

Next episode: Properties of Alkanes. Why does cooking gas burn, and what does chlorine do to methane in sunlight?
